crop.notes: The clipping is a run of political items: 'Brewster and Swanger Address Large Audience', 'Many Register From One Small Building', 'Republican Primaries To-Day', 'Bay State Congressional Nominees' and part of the 'Levelers' (C. W. Post) advertisement. Only 'Many Register From One Small Building' mentions Allen, and it is complete.

ocr.notes: The Allen item is readable ('61) Market street' for 619, 'nest ei' for 'nest egg', 'Pines' for 'place'); the surrounding items have many errors.

title.suggested: 102 Voters Registered From Tom Allen's Old Saloon Building

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat reported that Republican clerks copying the registration books found 102 voters registered from the small two-story building at 619 Market Street, whose ground floor had been Tom Allen's saloon.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Wednesday Morning, October 5, 1904, page 11. The item also says John L. Sullivan was employed in the place but was not among those registered.

facts.fact: The lower floor of the two-story building at 619 Market Street, St. Louis, had formerly been Allen's saloon

notes: The current summary calls 619 Market Street 'Tom Allen's address'; the article says only that the ground floor was formerly his saloon.
